questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why women face special difficulties in politics
How to become a prime minister
The history of the Conservative party
Why men are better political leaders
questions.why: Neil says they'll be asking: why is life so hard for women in politics?

questions.q: What percentage of the world's politicians are women?
options: Over half
About 45%
Only 26%
About 10%
questions.why: Beth says only 26% of the world's politicians are women.

questions.q: What was partly behind Jacinda Ardern's resignation, according to Neil?
options: A scandal about how her party spent money
Online abuse aimed at her as a woman
Losing an election to the other party
Arguments with her own party about taxes
questions.why: He says it was partly because of the misogynistic abuse she received online.

questions.q: According to Professor Rosie Campbell, how was Margaret Thatcher coached?
options: To dress and walk like a man in parliament
To speak more softly and kindly to voters
To avoid speaking in public whenever possible
To act more like a man but dress like a woman
questions.why: She was coached to change her voice and behave more masculine, while dressing in a very feminine way.

questions.q: What does Neil say about how women in politics are treated today?
options: Their clothes and manners are judged more
They are treated in exactly the same way as men
The internet has made things much easier for them
Nobody comments on their clothes or appearance
questions.why: He says the way women behave or dress is commented on and criticised far more than men.

questions.q: Why is it described as a paradox?
options: Women vote more often but win fewer elections
Men are usually more caring than women
Politics needs 'female' qualities but has few women
Most politicians don't like empathy or kindness
questions.why: Beth says empathy and understanding, often linked with women, are most needed in politics today.

questions.q: What leadership style does Helen Clark link with women?
options: Strict, top-down and not open to other views
Working together and open to debate
Fast, emotional and unpredictable
Quiet, careful and avoiding hard decisions
questions.why: She says women are known for more collaborative styles and are more open to evidenced debate.

questions.q: What does Beth suggest about leaders like Margaret Thatcher and Liz Truss?
options: They were too collaborative with other parties
They were forced out by men in their own party
They were the most successful leaders in history
Their very strict style helped end their time
questions.why: She says adopting dictatorial approaches has been the end of many leaders, including them.
